Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

I help buyers find top-floor penthouse condos across Langley, from the newer towers in Willoughby to the buildings near downtown Langley City. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and a member of the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's Medallion Club for 10 straight years, which puts me in the top 1% of all Realtors in the Fraser Valley by FVREB sales. I've also closed more than $500M in sales.

This page shows penthouse condos for sale across Langley. The feed uses the Penthouse style tag that listing agents add on MLS®, so it shows top-floor apartments the agent has marked as a penthouse. If you want to see every apartment instead, start with my
Langley condos for sale
page.

A penthouse has no legal definition in BC. On MLS®, the listing agent picks it as a style for a unit, normally one at the top of an apartment building. A penthouse may fill an entire floor, or it may sit on the top floor alongside a few other units. Some have a private roof deck, a larger deck or higher ceilings, though the name promises none of these.

Because the agent chooses the tag, some top-floor units never get it, while a few listings have PH in the unit number but lack the tag. So that a good unit doesn't slip past you, I weigh the floor, the unit number and the tag as a set.

Willoughby is in the Township of Langley, so zoning and permits come from the Township. Most of its apartment buildings are newer, and top-floor units there are often in mid-rise buildings near the shops. Browse every apartment on my
Willoughby condos for sale
page.

The City of Langley is its own city, separate from the Township, with its own zoning and building bylaws. Its apartment buildings sit around downtown near Fraser Highway and 203 Street. Browse every apartment on my
City of Langley condos for sale
page.

I grew up on a farm in Langley and live here again now. A top-floor unit can feel very different from the one below it, so I like to visit at different times of day to check light, noise and the view from the deck itself.
Because a penthouse is a strata lot, the strata corporation and BC's Strata Property Act both apply to you. A top-floor unit raises some extra questions that lower floors don't.
Roof decks.

Roof decks are frequently limited common property, which is common property reserved for a single unit's use rather than being part of the unit. The strata plan and bylaws set out who may use it, which items it can hold and who pays to maintain it.
The roof over your head.
The roof sits right above a penthouse, so read the depreciation report for the roof, membrane and elevator plans, then recent minutes for leaks, special levies or repairs.
Strata fees.

The Form B Information Certificate lists the exact monthly fee, any special levies and which bylaws are in force. Unit entitlement, which appears on the strata plan, normally drives the fees, and bigger units tend to hold more entitlement, which means a higher monthly fee.

1. What makes a condo a penthouse on MLS?
A penthouse is, in practice, a top-floor unit that its listing agent gave the Penthouse style. The term has no legal definition, so check the floor and layout for yourself.
2. Where are most Langley penthouses?
Most are in Willoughby and Langley City, where most of Langley's apartment buildings are.
3. Are Willoughby and Langley City under the same city rules?
No. Willoughby is in the Township of Langley. The City of Langley is a separate city with its own zoning and building bylaws.
4. Is a penthouse roof deck mine alone?
Often not. A lot of roof decks are limited common property reserved for one unit, and the strata plan and bylaws state who uses it and who covers upkeep.
5. Do penthouse owners pay higher strata fees?
Fees generally follow unit entitlement, so a bigger unit often carries more entitlement and a higher fee. The Form B states the exact monthly amount.
6. What strata documents should I read?

Documents to review: the bylaws and rules, recent minutes, the financial statements, the depreciation report and the Form B Information Certificate. Roof, membrane and elevator items are what to look for.
7. Can I search for PH unit numbers instead?
A unit number such as PH1 is a useful clue, yet some penthouses don't use one and some top-floor units aren't tagged. In each case I weigh the floor, the tag and the unit number against each other.
